# @arki/journal

> A journal for Drizzle entities. Every change is one normal table row and, when the entity's events are stored (the default), one immutable event row, written in one transaction. Projections run inside that transaction. Effects run after the commit, from a job table.

## Import paths

<!-- llms:start -->
- `@arki/journal`: `BATCH_LIMIT`, `COMMAND_FAILURES`, `CommandConflict`, `CommandForbidden`, `CommandInvalid`, `CommandNotFound`, `JournalError`, `RUN_FIELD_LIMITS`, `WorkflowBusy`, `WorkflowReadMismatch`, `WorkflowStranded`, `backoff`; and 141 more.
- http/* (2 paths): The HTTP response cache on Postgres: `@arki/http/idempotency` stores a finished response here and replays it when the same `Idempotency-Key` comes again. `@arki/journal/http`, `@arki/journal/http/webhooks`.
- one path each: `@arki/journal/pg`, `@arki/journal/foreman`, `@arki/journal/dot`, `@arki/journal/errors`, `@arki/journal/contract`, `@arki/journal/orpc`, `@arki/journal/projection`, `@arki/journal/testing`, `@arki/journal/event-log-contract`, `@arki/journal/postgres`, `@arki/journal/kurrentdb`, `@arki/journal/zod`.
<!-- llms:end -->

## By task
- [Add an event and react in the same transaction](docs/agent-guide.md#add-an-event-and-react-in-the-same-transaction)
- [Add an entity with create and delete](docs/agent-guide.md#add-an-entity-with-create-and-delete)
- [Add an effect that runs after commit](docs/agent-guide.md#add-an-effect-that-runs-after-commit)
- [Add a command and run it](docs/agent-guide.md#add-a-command-and-run-it)
- [Schedule a job in the same transaction](docs/agent-guide.md#schedule-a-job-in-the-same-transaction)
- Run jobs scheduled by `@arki/queue/outbox`: give `journal.worker(db, { jobs })` or `journalWorker({ jobs })` a runner. See [Queue jobs in the jobs table](README.md#queue-jobs-in-the-jobs-table)
- [Operate and retain jobs](docs/agent-guide.md#operate-and-retain-jobs): states, paged reads, verbs with `op`, retention, archive sink. Long form: [Operating the jobs](README.md#operating-the-jobs) and [Retention and archive](README.md#retention-and-archive)
- Inbox and relay recipes: [Inbox](README.md#inbox), [Relay recipe](README.md#relay-recipe)
- [Add a durable workflow](docs/agent-guide.md#workflows): steps, waits, undo, versions, operators, `workflowHarness`. Long form: [Workflows](README.md#workflows). Must survive a restart or wait for hours → `j.workflow`; steps inside one request → `createFlow` from `@arki/ai`
- Keep events in another store (another Postgres, an event store): `j.entity(kind, table, { events: log })`. See [Events in another store](README.md#events-in-another-store)
- Keep only the row, no events: `j.entity(kind, table, { events: 'transient' })`, or `initJournal({ tables, events: 'transient' })` for every entity. See [Transient events](README.md#transient-events)
- [Find out why a write failed](docs/agent-guide.md#find-out-why-a-write-failed), with the [error table](docs/agent-guide.md#errors) and the [recovery verbs](docs/agent-guide.md#recovery-verbs)
- [Wire it in a Dot app](docs/agent-guide.md#dot), or [ship journal pieces from a shared package](docs/agent-guide.md#shared-packages)

## Rules that bite
- The door is `journal.bind(db, meta)`: bind once per request or job, then call `run(command, input)`. You give `meta`; the library never picks an actor.
- A rule that rejects a request returns a failure (`CommandNotFound({ detail })` and the others, or the app's own). The command rolls back exactly as for a throw, and `journal.run` returns it, typed. An `events` failure comes back from `write`, a child's from `run`: return it from the handler. A command that got one and still returns a success throws `IGNORED_FAILURE` and commits nothing. To handle a refusal on purpose, check it and call `accept(result)` (on the command and the effect context): it lifts only this command's check, once per return of that very value; the refused child stays rolled back. Misuse throws `INVALID_ACCEPT`. A failure is not a `JournalError`. An oRPC app adds `commandErrors()` once, after its own error middleware; it answers a returned failure as an error too.
- A command declares its events: `j.command(name, input, { writes: [OrderPaid] }, handler)`. `write` takes only those; an undeclared event that gets past the types fails with `BAD_DEFINITION` and nothing commits.
- Await every `write` and `run`. One journal operation per transaction at a time. No `Promise.all` over writes.
- `drain` and `worker` take the root database, never a transaction.
- An effect that needs a service lists it: `j.effect(name, entity, { mailer: need<Mailer>() }, on)`. The handler reads `mailer` from its context. A plain app gives the services once, in `j.compose({ services })`. In a Dot feature the effect picks them with `needsOf((_: Deps) => ['mailer'])`, as a plain exported value with `import type { Deps }` from the feature, and is mounted with `.usecases({}, journalHandlers(core, { effects }))`.
- Any running worker can claim any job. Run the worker in the process that holds what its effects talk to (for example an in-memory emitter).
- A reducer returns the value the database will store, or the write fails with `VALUE_MISMATCH`. Returning `null` deletes the row. A soft delete is a normal patch.
- Version 1 means created by the journal. A row that existed before the journal starts at version 2. `adopt` takes a row at any version with no history and makes it version 1; that is also how an entity goes from `events: 'transient'` to `'stored'`.
- Events are stored unless the entity says `events: 'transient'`. A transient entity still gets reducers, inline projections and effects; async projections and taps on it are refused at `compose`, and replay, verify, repair, forget, rerun and adopt throw `NO_HISTORY`. `workflow.run` always stores its events.
- `events` also takes an event log. One that cannot join the transaction is forwarded: a `forward` job appends the events after the commit, one entity's jobs in version order. History verbs throw `FORWARD_PENDING` until it ran; `journal.forwardLag(db)` shows what waits. Test an adapter with `eventLogContract` from `@arki/journal/event-log-contract`.
- `postgresEvents({ db, tables: eventLogTables() })` from `@arki/journal/postgres` keeps events in another Postgres database, with `all` and `erase`. To switch an entity's store: pause its writes, `journal.copyLog(db, entity, { to })`, flip `events`, `reset` its async projections.
- `kurrentEvents({ client, prefix? })` from `@arki/journal/kurrentdb` keeps events in KurrentDB: one stream per entity (`<kind>-<id>`, no `-` in the kind), `all` over `$all`, no `forget`.
- Pass ids exactly as they are stored. Events are frozen: copy before you change.
- A workflow step runs at least once. The step body owns idempotency: pass `ctx.key` to the provider. Compose workflows once per `initJournal()`.
- An effect has no `run`. An event that must run a command starts a `j.task` or a `j.workflow` with `startOn`. `startOn.timing` is required: `'after-commit'`, or `'with-event'` (the run is written in the event's transaction; `onBusy: 'refuse'` does not compile).
- A `.command(name, command, ({ input, results }) => commandInput, { accept?, undo?, when?, retry? })` node commits the command with its checkpoint: exactly once. Its result comes from the command's `output` schema.

> The design spec (`docs/specs/2026-10-09-journal-design.md`) explains intent. `src/api.ts` defines the signatures. When they differ, `src/api.ts` is right.
